scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8874: After a change window this morning, host_2_1_1_1 lost
all connectivity beyond its gateway 10.2.1.1 -- the server farm and pod 1
both time out. Monitoring shows switch_dist_2_1 now has NO OSPF neighbors:
its adjacency to router_core_2 dropped and never re-formed, yet the physical
uplink interface still shows UP on both ends. Pod 1 and the server farm are
otherwise healthy. Find what broke the adjacency.

injection.action: move the core-facing uplink network into the wrong OSPF area (area 0 instead of area 1)
injection.command:
vtysh -c "configure terminal" \
        -c "router ospf" \
        -c "no network 172.16.0.8/31 area 1" \
        -c "network 172.16.0.8/31 area 0" \
        -c "exit" -c "exit"
  vtysh -c "clear ip ospf process"

post_inject_check.command: vtysh -c "show ip ospf neighbor" | grep -c Full

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch_dist_2_1 OSPF area assignment on the uplink
  network 172.16.0.8/31
Mechanism: OSPF requires both ends of a link to agree on the area ID.
  router_core_2's side of the 172.16.0.8/31 uplink is in area 1;
  switch_dist_2_1's side was just moved to area 0. Hellos now carry
  mismatched area IDs and are rejected in both directions, so the adjacency
  never re-forms even though the link is physically UP. With its only
  adjacency gone, switch_dist_2_1 learns no remote routes and pod 2
  (10.2.1.0/24) is isolated; the rest of the network also withdraws pod 2's
  prefix once router_core_2 stops hearing switch_dist_2_1's LSAs.
Localization: switch_dist_2_1
Root cause: OSPF area mismatch on the router_core_2<->switch_dist_2_1 uplink
  (switch_dist_2_1 in area 0, router_core_2 in area 1)
Fix: restore area 1 on switch_dist_2_1 (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
On switch_dist_2_1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router ospf" -c "no network 172.16.0.8/31 area 0" -c "network 172.16.0.8/31 area 1"`
(`service frr restart` also heals it: the change was made only to the running
config, and /etc/frr/frr.conf still has the correct area-1 statement.)
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: OSPF area assignment / area mismatch on the uplink (area 0 vs area 1)
must-identify-mechanism: hello area-ID mismatch prevents the adjacency from re-forming while the link stays physically UP
bonus-rules-out-physical: explicitly notes the uplink is UP on both ends, distinguishing the config fault from a cable/interface failure

line.command: vtysh -c "show ip ospf neighbor" | grep -c Full

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: OSPF adjacency on the uplink between distribution switch switch_dist_2_1 and core router router_core_2.

Mechanism: OSPF neighbors only form when key parameters match, including the area ID. Today the two ends of the point-to-point /31 link disagree on the OSPF area, so they continuously ignore each other’s hellos and never reach 2-Way/Full. With no adjacency, switch_dist_2_1 learns no inter-area routes and can only route its connected 10.2.1.0/24 subnet; hosts behind it can reach the gateway (10.2.1.1) but nothing beyond.

Localization: The link is 172.16.0.8/31 on router_core_2:eth2 <-> 172.16.0.9/31 on switch_dist_2_1:eth0. Direct evidence:
- switch_dist_2_1 “show ip ospf interface eth0” shows Area 0.0.0.0 and Neighbor Count 0; its OSPF config has “network 172.16.0.8/31 area 0”.
- router_core_2 “show ip ospf interface eth2” shows Area 0.0.0.1 and Neighbor Count 0; its OSPF config has “network 172.16.0.8/31 area 1”.
- Physical link is up on both ends (eth0/eth2 are UP with 172.16.0.9/31 and 172.16.0.8/31 respectively).

Root cause: During the change window, router_core_2’s eth2 was placed in OSPF area 1 while switch_dist_2_1’s matching interface remained in area 0, creating an OSPF area mismatch on the 172.16.0.8/31 link.

Corrective fix: Restore matching OSPF areas on both ends. Per design (core as backbone), change router_core_2 to put 172.16.0.8/31 back in area 0:
- On router_core_2: remove “network 172.16.0.8/31 area 1” and add “network 172.16.0.8/31 area 0”. Verify “show ip ospf neighbor” reaches Full on both devices and that routes to remote subnets return on switch_dist_2_1.

per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly names and localizes switch_dist_2_1 (shows eth0, area 0 and Neighbor Count 0) as the affected device.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies an OSPF area mismatch on the 172.16.0.8/31 uplink, noting switch_dist_2_1 in area 0 and router_core_2 in area 1.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states the physical link is up on both interfaces (eth0/eth2 are UP with IPs), distinguishing a config area mismatch from a cable/interface failure.
The agent recommends changing router_core_2 to area 0 instead of restoring switch_dist_2_1 to area 1 (or restarting FRR), which contradicts the expected fix to make the switch match the core.

Interface and OSPF-interface outputs in the log explicitly show the two ends have different area IDs and zero adjacency, and the writeup’s inference (area mismatch broke the adjacency causing routing loss) follows directly from those observations. The suggested remediation picks the opposite side to change (not justified by config/design in the log) but does not weaken the core diagnosis.
